headline: ICT complaints seek probe into Mohammed Shahabuddin's role in July Uprising
summary: Complaints filed by Rastrosonglap Forum and Bangladesh Azad Party allege the former president's silence and inaction during the July 2024 Uprising.
details: Two separate complaints were filed with the Chief Prosecutor's Office of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) seeking an investigation into former president Mohammed Shahabuddin.
The complaints allege that Shahabuddin had a role in crimes against humanity and human rights violations committed during the July 2024 Uprising.
Al Nur Mohammad Ayash of the Rastrosonglap Forum urged the ICT to investigate whether the former president bore legal responsibility for killings, torture, and enforced disappearances.
The Bangladesh Azad Party (BAP) also filed a complaint, with President Brig Gen (retd) Hasinur Rahman stating that around 1,400 people were killed during the uprising.
Hasinur alleged that despite holding the highest constitutional office, Shahabuddin remained silent and took no action to prevent the violence.
ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam confirmed the receipt of of the complaints but stated he has not yet reviewed them.
caption:
Former president Mohammed Shahabuddin faces ICT complaints seeking a probe into his role in the July Uprising killings.

Two separate complaints were filed with the Chief Prosecutor's Office of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) seeking an investigation into former president Mohammed Shahabuddin.

The complaints allege that Shahabuddin had a role in crimes against humanity and human rights violations committed during the July 2024 Uprising.

Al Nur Mohammad Ayash of the Rastrosonglap Forum urged the ICT to investigate whether the former president bore legal responsibility for killings, torture, and enforced disappearances.

The Bangladesh Azad Party (BAP) also filed a complaint, with President Brig Gen (retd) Hasinur Rahman stating that around 1,400 people were killed during the uprising.

Hasinur alleged that despite holding the highest constitutional office, Shahabuddin remained silent and took no action to prevent the violence.

ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam confirmed the receipt of of the complaints but stated he has not yet reviewed them.

Source: Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline: Two former presidents complaints filed against former presidents at ICT
summary: The Bangladesh Azadi Party and Rashtrasanglap Forum have filed complaints with the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against former presidents Abdul Hamid and Mohammed Shahabuddin.
details: Two organizations, the Bangladesh Azadi Party and Rashtrasanglap Forum, have filed separate complaints with the Chief Prosecutor's office of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against former presidents Mohammed Shahabuddin and Abdul Hamid.

The Bangladesh Azadi Party alleged that the former presidents gave their silent consent to killings, disappearances, and other atrocities during their tenure, effectively supporting the fascist government.

The complaints include allegations of involvement in the event known as the Pilkhana massacre, the Shapla Square massacre, judicial killings, and the operation of 'Aynaghar' (House of Mirrors) torture centers.
The Rashtrasanglap Forum filed a complaint specifically against former president Mohammed Shahabuddin, alleging he was a close associate of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
The forum's complaint against Shahabuddin also seeks an investigation into his role as an 'order-giver' for the shooting, torture, and killings of students and people during the July uprising.
The forum also demands a fair and independent investigation into Shahabuddin's legal liability or involvement in the 2024 national elections and other human rights violations.
When questioned by journalists, the Chief Prosecutor of the ICT, Aminul Islam, declined to comment on the the complaints filed against the former presidents.
The complaints are now with the ICT Chief Prosecutor's office for review and potential further action.
caption:
Former presidents Abdul Hamid and Mohammed Shahabuddin are facing ICT complaints for their alleged roles in mass killings and human rights violations.

Two organizations, the Bangladesh Azadi Party and Rashtrasanglap Forum, have filed separate complaints with the Chief Prosecutor's office of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against former presidents Mohammed Shahabuddin and Abdul Hamid.

The Bangladesh Azadi Party alleged that the former presidents gave their silent consent to killings, disappearances, and other atrocities during their tenure, effectively supporting the fascist government.

The complaints include allegations of involvement in the event known as the Pilkhana massacre, the Shapla Square massacre, judicial killings, and the operation of 'Aynaghar' (House of Mirrors) torture centers.

The Rashtrasanglap Forum filed a complaint specifically against former president Mohammed Shahabuddin, alleging he was a close associate of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

The forum's complaint against Shahabuddin also seeks an investigation into his role as an 'order-giver' for the shooting, torture, and killings of students and people during the July uprising.

The forum also demands a fair and independent investigation into Shahabuddin's legal liability or involvement in the 2024 national elections and other human rights violations.

When questioned by journalists, the Chief Prosecutor of the ICT, Aminul Islam, declined to comment on the the complaints filed against the former presidents.

The complaints are now with the ICT Chief Prosecutor's office for review and potential further action.

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune
